newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends at $19 high as U.S gasoline rallies.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends at $19 high as U.S gasoline rallies.

text.p: IPE Brent crude jumped to close at an eight-week high on Wednesday as U.S. gasoline prices rallied again on the back of supportive inventory data.
September Brent closed up 41 cents at $19.00 a barrel, the highest level for the prompt contract since June 3.
Gains of over three cents a gallon on prompt NYMEX unleaded gasoline futures were the main factor, brokers said.
"Short-term gasoline is pretty tight in the U.S. and people are having to pay up," said a broker.
The American Petroleum Institute (API) and the U.S. Department of Energy said gasoline stocks fell by over three million barrels last week.
News that Tosco Corp had been forced on Wednesday to shut down the catalytic cracking unit at its Bayway refinery after the discovery of a leak gave the rally fresh impetus, brokers said.
The New Jersey unit, which usually produces about 130,000 bpd of gasoline, could be out of action for two weeks, a source close to the refinery said.
Crude markets were also drawing their own support from U.S. data showing stocks fell by nearly 10 million barrels last week.

But some analysts, pointing to a steady level of crude imports and a slight decline in refinery operating rates, said the decline may have been due to the short-term impact of Hurricane Danny which forced the temporary closure of some fields in the Gulf of Mexico.
Brent's rally was also tempered by concern that U.N. approval of Baghdad's aid distribution plan, expected shortly, could release a massive wave of Iraqi exports by mid-August.
Some of Iraq's closest trading allies were confident on Wednesday that Iraqi crude exports are set to resume shortly.
Earlier, IPE Aug gas oil closed $3.25 firmer at $171.00 a tonne. -- Mark Thompson, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7930
